options.text: Semaglutide ages the face by acting on facial fat, so the label should carry a facial warning.

Facial volume loss on incretins: fat loss deflates facial compartments (mechanism); small observational studies tie it to the amount of weight lost (human evidence); US labels list hair loss but not facial change (regulatory status); whether the drugs act directly on facial fat is untested (open question).
Weight loss on these drugs is GRADE A, so their facial effects are GRADE A too.

modules.title: Matrix peptides and wound healing
modules.objective: By the end, you can critique the biological plausibility, transdermal penetration barriers, and human clinical evidence for cosmetic, matrikine, and investigational tissue-repair peptides.

blocks.title: The peptide your patient already bought.
blocks.narration: Most skin peptides reach your clinic before any evidence does. In three lessons you will sort them by what the human trials actually show, who paid for those trials, and where each one stands with the regulator.

blocks.title: Matrix peptides and wound healing
blocks.sourceNote: Pickart & Thaler 1973 · Pickart 2008, 2015, 2018 · Peptide Pocket Guide

blocks.title: How will you use this module?
blocks.narration: The evidence and grades are the same for everyone, and regulatory notes follow the country you choose. What changes with your role is the 'what you do next' at the end of each lesson, so it fits what your licence lets you do.

blocks.title: A plasma tripeptide with a copper habit.
blocks.narration: Start with the molecule. GHK is a three-amino-acid peptide that circulates in human plasma; it was first described in 1973. It binds copper readily, and the copper complex, GHK-Cu, is what skin-care labels mean when they say copper peptide. The proposed mechanism is that GHK-Cu delivers copper to enzymes that build and protect the dermal matrix, such as lysyl oxidase and superoxide dismutase, and shifts gene expression toward wound healing. Two things to hold on to. First, this is a mechanism, which explains why the peptide might work and leaves open whether it does. Second, most of this literature was written by the group that discovered the peptide. Keep both in mind when you reach the trials.
blocks.sourceNote: Pickart & Thaler 1973 · Pickart 2008, 2015, 2018 · Peptide Pocket Guide

blocks.title: One indexed randomized trial.
blocks.narration: A search of PubMed in September 2026 found one randomized controlled trial of topical GHK-Cu in human skin: 2006, healing after CO₂ laser resurfacing. The cosmetic trials cited for anti-ageing claims are manufacturer-sponsored and not indexed. Both Hormonaly guides grade topical use C.
blocks.sourceNote: Miller 2006 · Peptide Pocket Guide · Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology

stat.label: indexed randomized trial of topical GHK-Cu in human skin

blocks.title: Keep the four answers apart.
blocks.narration: Every peptide question has four separate answers. For GHK-Cu they point in different directions, which is exactly why they must not be blended into one sentence.
blocks.sourceNote: FDA 503A category list, updated 14 May 2026

blocks.title: Serum yes, syringe no.
blocks.narration: Here is what that means in the room. Topical GHK-Cu is a reasonable cosmetic conversation, as long as you describe the evidence honestly: small trials, modest effects, grade C. Injected GHK-Cu is not the same product in a stronger form. There are no randomized trials of injection, injection-site pain and rash are common because copper irritates tissue, and in the United States the injectable route sits outside the Category 1 listing that covers non-injectable use. Whatever your role, name the route every time you talk about this peptide.
blocks.sourceNote: Peptide Pocket Guide · Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology, ch. 15 · FDA 503A categories

blocks.narration: One question to close lesson 4.1.
blocks.sourceNote: Lesson 4.1

quiz.prompt: A patient asks whether GHK-Cu injections are 'stronger' than the serum she uses. What does the evidence support?

blocks.title: Three families, one question: who ran the trial?
blocks.narration: Lesson two covers three families that fill the cosmetic and supplement shelves. Signal peptides, like palmitoyl pentapeptide-4, sold as Matrixyl, are fragments of matrix proteins meant to tell fibroblasts to make more collagen. SNAP-25 mimics, Argireline and its longer cousin SNAP-8, copy part of a nerve-terminal protein that botulinum toxin targets; the idea is a gentle, topical version of that effect. And oral collagen peptides are swallowed, not applied. Every one of these has trials behind it. As you go through them, keep asking one question before any other: who ran the trial, and who paid for it.
blocks.sourceNote: Lupo & Cole 2007 · Lintner & Peschard 2000 · Blanes-Mira 2002 · Errante 2020

blocks.title: A trial, or a brochure?
blocks.narration: Five products from two families, and what each promises on the label. Before you see a grade, decide what actually stands behind each one.
blocks.sourceNote: Robinson 2005 · Wang 2013 · Aruan 2023 · Errante 2020 · Pocket Guide

blocks.title: Twenty-three trials, split by who paid.
blocks.narration: Pooled, oral collagen trials show better hydration, elasticity and wrinkle scores, and the Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide grades them C. A 2025 meta-analysis split the same kind of trials by funding and by quality. The benefit appeared only in pharmaceutical-funded and low-quality trials. Unfunded and high-quality trials showed no effect.
blocks.sourceNote: Myung & Park, Am J Med 2025 · Pu 2023 · de Miranda 2021 · Kim 2018

stat.label: in the 2025 meta-analysis that split oral-collagen trials by funding and quality

blocks.title: Cosmetic, supplement, drug: three rulebooks.
blocks.narration: Now the regulatory register, stated for the United States. Cosmetic peptides are cosmetic ingredients, not drugs; their safety is assessed under a cosmetics framework, and nobody has to prove they work before they are sold. Oral collagen is sold as a dietary supplement, so it cannot claim to treat a disease, and what is in the tub varies from brand to brand. That is the whole reason the funding question matters here. When no regulator asks for efficacy, the only efficacy data are the trials someone chose to pay for.
blocks.sourceNote: Bjerke 2026 · Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology · Pocket Guide

blocks.title: 'Clinically proven' collagen.
blocks.narration: One question to close lesson 4.2.
blocks.sourceNote: Lesson 4.2

quiz.prompt: A patient shows you a collagen drink labelled 'clinically proven to reduce wrinkles'. What is the most accurate reply?

blocks.title: Rodents, a fragment, and a tripeptide.
blocks.narration: Lesson three moves from the cosmetic shelf to the peptides patients buy online and inject. BPC-157 is a fifteen-residue peptide first described in 1993. Its evidence is a large rodent literature, most of it from one research group, and uncontrolled human case series. TB-500 is sold as thymosin, but when anti-doping chemists analysed the product they found a seven-residue fragment, residues seventeen to twenty-three of thymosin beta-four. That fragment has never been tested in a trial. KPV is the last three amino acids of alpha-MSH; it calms inflammation in mouse colitis models, and there is no randomized human trial of it for anything. All three have plausible mechanisms, and none has a controlled human trial.
blocks.sourceNote: Sikiric 2018 · Seiwerth 2021 · Lee 2021 · Esposito 2012 · Dalmasso 2008

blocks.title: One abstract, no published trial.
blocks.narration: As of September 2026 no randomized efficacy trial of BPC-157 in people has been published in full. FDA's July 2026 briefing found one randomized, placebo-controlled trial reported only as a 2005 meeting abstract: 53 people with ulcerative colitis, two weeks of treatment, and no significant difference from placebo. ClinicalTrials.gov adds a 2015 phase 1 safety study that never posted results, a completed 2025 single-arm product study with no results posted, and a randomized phase 1 trial after rotator-cuff surgery due to start in 2027.
blocks.sourceNote: ClinicalTrials.gov, checked 24 Sep 2026 · McGuire 2025 · Mayfield 2026

stat.label: randomized efficacy trials of BPC-157 in people published in full (September 2026)

blocks.title: Two trials, one peptide: LL-37.
blocks.narration: LL-37, the skin's own cathelicidin, is the one repair peptide with two randomized trials in hard-to-heal venous leg ulcers. Read them in order.
blocks.sourceNote: Grönberg 2014 · Mahlapuu 2021 · Schauber & Gallo 2008

blocks.title: Where does it stand in the US?
blocks.narration: Three US categories, dated to the FDA's category list of 14 May 2026 and the advisory-committee meeting of 23–24 July 2026. The committee's votes are advice; FDA must still act through rulemaking before anything joins the bulks list. FDA has sent warning letters naming GHK-Cu and BPC-157 on exactly this basis.
blocks.sourceNote: FDA 503A categories (14 May 2026) · 91 FR 20465 · PCAC 23–24 Jul 2026 · FDA warning letter 2020

blocks.title: New dark patches, three months into 'GLOW'.
blocks.narration: A fictional case, built from this lesson's evidence. A forty-six-year-old patient has been injecting a research-use-only blend sold as GLOW for three months: GHK-Cu, BPC-157 and TB-500 in one vial. She likes her skin and asks about carrying on. You notice new, patchy darkening on her face and forearms. The blend has no controlled human trials, it is made outside good manufacturing practice, and the Hormonaly guide treats new pigmentation on these products as a red flag. Impurity and mislabelling are documented for similar online products; the Hormonaly guide states that heavy-metal contamination is documented in these products, but the published analysis behind that statement could not be found. Decide what you do first.
blocks.sourceNote: Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology, ch. 15 · Pocket Guide · Vanhee 2020 · Ashraf 2024

modules.title: Follicle, pigment and melanocortins
modules.objective: By the end, you can appraise the neuroendocrinology of the hair follicle and melanocortin receptor system, contrasting FDA-approved therapeutics with the clinical and oncologic hazards of unregulated peptides.

blocks.title: A spray for the scalp, a tan in a vial.
blocks.narration: Two requests reach aesthetic clinics well ahead of their evidence: a peptide to regrow hair and an injection to tan. In three lessons you will see how the follicle and the pigment system run on the skin's own hormones, why one melanocortin drug is approved while its gray-market cousin is approved nowhere, and how to grade the hair peptides patients bring to you.

blocks.title: Follicle, pigment and melanocortins
blocks.sourceNote: Ito 2005 · Horesh 2023 · Bertolini 2020 · Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology, ch. 6

blocks.title: A follicle that runs its own hormones.
blocks.narration: Each hair follicle behaves like a small gland. When researchers keep human scalp follicles alive in culture, the follicles answer corticotropin-releasing hormone the way the pituitary and adrenal glands do. They make ACTH and alpha-MSH, they secrete cortisol, and cortisol-like signals feed back to switch the stimulus down. The same follicles run a growth hormone and IGF-1 loop of their own. On the scalp, an enzyme called five-alpha-reductase turns testosterone into dihydrotestosterone, and in genetically susceptible follicles that hormone drives the gradual shrinking behind pattern hair loss. Growing follicles also hide from the immune system. When that protection collapses, immune cells attack the hair bulb, and the result is alopecia areata. Most of this biology comes from tissue kept alive outside the body, so hold it as mechanism, a reason something might matter in patients.
blocks.sourceNote: Ito 2005 · Horesh 2023 · Bertolini 2020 · Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology, ch. 6

blocks.title: Two trials, 1,200 adults, one approval.
blocks.narration: When immune privilege fails, the attack depends on cytokine signals that JAK inhibitors interrupt. Two randomized phase 3 trials tested oral baricitinib in 1,200 adults with severe alopecia areata. In the US, FDA approved baricitinib for adults with severe alopecia areata on 13 June 2022. The Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide grades it A.
blocks.sourceNote: King 2022 (BRAVE-AA1 and -AA2) · FDA approval letter, 13 Jun 2022

stat.label: adults with severe alopecia areata in the two phase 3 trials of baricitinib (2022)

blocks.title: Four questions before any product.
blocks.narration: The Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide's first-pass hair-loss workup asks four questions in order. Each yes points to a different condition and a different next step.
blocks.sourceNote: Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology · hair-loss workup algorithm and ch. 5 referral list

blocks.title: Work up the hair loss before anyone mentions a peptide.
blocks.narration: Most requests for a hair peptide skip the diagnosis. Start with the pattern, ask about a trigger, look for patches and nail pitting, and look for signs of androgen excess. Check ferritin and thyroid function every time, and send a scarring pattern for biopsy. The approved options already carry strong evidence. Pooled randomized trials support topical minoxidil in men and women and finasteride in men. In the United States minoxidil is sold over the counter, while finasteride for hair loss needs a prescription. Severe or fast-spreading alopecia areata belongs with a dermatologist, where a JAK inhibitor is an approved option for adults. Whatever your role, the workup comes before the product.
blocks.sourceNote: Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology · Adil 2017 · Drugs@FDA (checked 24 Sep 2026) · FDA approval letter 2022

blocks.title: Shedding after the baby.
blocks.narration: One question to close lesson 5.1.
blocks.sourceNote: Lesson 5.1

quiz.prompt: A 32-year-old woman asks for a compounded peptide scalp spray. Diffuse shedding began three months after she gave birth; there are no patches and no signs of androgen excess. What comes first?

blocks.title: Five receptors, one family of hormones.
blocks.narration: Pigment starts with hormones the skin makes for itself. Skin cells produce a precursor called POMC and cut it into ACTH, alpha-MSH and beta-endorphin, and the same cells carry the receptors that answer them. There are five melanocortin receptors. MC1R sets the pigment of skin and hair. MC2R is the adrenal receptor for ACTH. MC3R and MC4R work in the brain on appetite, and central receptors also drive sexual responses. MC5R governs sebum. Researchers caution that the real map is messier, with receptors turning up in more tissues than the textbook suggests. For this lesson one idea matters most. A drug that stays on MC1R mostly changes pigment, and a drug that reaches the brain's receptors brings other effects with it.
blocks.sourceNote: Slominski & Wortsman 2000 · Laiho & Murray 2022 · Böhm 2025

blocks.title: One receptor family, two very different molecules.
blocks.narration: Afamelanotide and Melanotan II are both synthetic relatives of α-MSH. Compare them register by register and the resemblance ends at the receptor.
blocks.sourceNote: Langendonk 2015 · EMA Scenesse EPAR · FDA Scenesse label (Aug 2024) · Dorr 1996 · Wessells 1998 · Böhm 2025

blocks.title: Sixty-nine hours against forty-one.
blocks.narration: Erythropoietic protoporphyria (EPP) is a rare disorder in which sunlight causes acute, severe pain. In the US phase 3 trial, adults on afamelanotide spent a median 69.4 hours in direct sunlight without pain over six months, against 40.8 hours on placebo. The European trial also showed more pain-free time and fewer phototoxic reactions. Both trials were funded by the manufacturer.
blocks.sourceNote: Langendonk 2015 (NEJM) · FDA Scenesse label, Aug 2024 · EMA EPAR

stat.label: median pain-free hours in direct sunlight over six months, afamelanotide vs placebo (US phase 3 trial, 94 adults with EPP)

blocks.title: What the case reports show.
blocks.narration: Now the harms, and the kind of evidence behind them. Everything here comes from case reports and reviews, which tell you what can happen and leave open how often it does. In the skin, existing moles darken and grow, new moles erupt in crops, some of them atypical under the microscope, and dark bands can appear in the nails. At least five melanomas have been reported during or after Melanotan use. Each patient had other risk factors, such as fair skin, sunbed use or a family history, so causation is unproven, and the concern rests on a drug that pushes melanocytes to multiply. Beyond the skin, reports describe priapism that needed surgery, a stimulant-like toxic reaction with muscle breakdown and kidney injury, and a brain swelling syndrome that FDA lists among the published serious events.
blocks.sourceNote: Habbema 2017 · Cardones 2009 · Paurobally 2013 · Hjuler 2014 · Mallory 2021 · Nelson 2012 · FDA compounding safety page

blocks.title: New moles after a summer of tanning shots.
blocks.narration: Her booking says skin quality. This patient is fictional, built from the lesson's evidence. She is twenty-seven, and she mentions that she has been injecting a tanning peptide bought online for three months. She has noticed darker moles, several new small ones, and a dark stripe along one fingernail. Her mother had melanoma. The product is almost certainly Melanotan II, approved nowhere and of unknown strength and purity. New and changing moles and nail pigmentation are exactly the harms described in the reports, and in one patient followed with dermoscopy the changes made moles hard to tell from melanoma. The endocrinology guide treats a family history of melanoma as an absolute contraindication. Pick the move that comes first.
blocks.sourceNote: Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology, ch. 15 · Cardones 2009 · Mang 2012 · Böhm 2025 · FDA Scenesse label

blocks.title: A Wnt switch and a zinc question.
blocks.narration: Two peptides are sold for hair, and both arrive with better stories than data. PTD-DBM joins a cell-penetrating fragment borrowed from an HIV protein to a short decoy sequence. Inside follicle cells, the decoy keeps a protein called CXXC5 from binding its partner, Dishevelled, and that releases a brake on Wnt signalling, a pathway involved in hair regrowth. In mice, hair regrew faster and follicles formed in healed wounds. The work came from the developer's own group. Zinc thymulin is a thymic hormone that becomes active only when zinc binds to it. How it might help hair has never been defined, and nobody has shown whether any effect would come from the peptide or from the zinc. Hold both as mechanism, and look for the human trial.
blocks.sourceNote: Lee 2017 (J Invest Dermatol) · Dardenne 1982 · Peptide Pocket Guide

blocks.title: Zero trials in people.
blocks.narration: As of September 2026, PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov list no human trial of PTD-DBM, published or registered. Its evidence is one 2017 study in mice and human scalp tissue from the developer's group, whose senior author is affiliated with a biotech company. A 2025 review's summary speaks of 'clinical efficacy', yet the review's own text describes PTD-DBM results in mouse models only.

blocks.title: When the request is a compounded hair spray.

On FDA's category lists of the fourteenth of May, twenty twenty-six, thymulin acetate sits in Category 3, meaning it was nominated without enough information for FDA to evaluate, and it falls outside the enforcement discretion that Category 1 substances receive. PTD-DBM appears on none of the three lists. Neither substance is on the 503A bulks list itself. The evidence grade for both is D. So when a patient asks for a compounded hair spray, give the grade plainly, go back to the diagnosis, and describe the approved options and what they can offer.

modules.title: The growth-hormone axis and the skin
modules.titleEn: The growth-hormone axis and the skin
modules.objective: By the end, you can analyze the impact of growth hormone and IGF-1 axis modulation on dermal architecture, collagen homeostasis, fluid dynamics, and mitogenic safety concerns.

units.title: The growth-hormone axis and the skin

blocks.title: Real endocrinology, borrowed for marketing.
blocks.narration: Growth hormone and IGF-1 genuinely shape skin, and one peptide on this axis has approval-grade trials. Most of what patients are offered has much less behind it. In three lessons you will separate the physiology from the promise, the approved from the anecdotal, and the side-effects you can see from the risks nobody has measured.

blocks.title: The growth-hormone axis and the skin
blocks.sourceNote: Tavakkol 1992 · Edmondson 2003 · Horesh 2023 · Veldhuis 2008 · Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology, ch. 2 and 6

blocks.title: Two hormones, two layers of skin.
blocks.narration: Two layers of skin listen to two different parts of the same axis. Growth hormone speaks mainly to the dermis. Its receptor is expressed more on fibroblasts than on keratinocytes, and in culture growth hormone increases fibroblast numbers and supports collagen synthesis, sometimes directly and sometimes through IGF-1. The epidermis listens to IGF-1. Keratinocytes carry the IGF-1 receptor, their neighbours in the dermis supply the hormone, and in culture IGF-1 makes keratinocytes divide where growth hormone on its own does nothing. Human hair follicles even keep a small growth-hormone loop running when they are cultured outside the body. With age, growth-hormone pulses and IGF-1 fall steadily, a change called the somatopause. Hold all of this as mechanism. It explains why the axis could matter for skin. Whether changing it helps a patient is a separate question, and the trials answer it.
blocks.sourceNote: Tavakkol 1992 · Edmondson 2003 · Horesh 2023 · Veldhuis 2008 · Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology, ch. 2 and 6

blocks.title: A much-cited skin result, read again.
blocks.narration: In 1990 a much-cited New England Journal of Medicine study gave growth hormone for six months to 12 healthy men over 60, with nine untreated men for comparison and no placebo. Lean mass rose and fat fell. Skin thickness rose 7.1%, with P = 0.07, short of statistical significance. A small 1996 randomized trial in 28 older men found 15% more collagen laid down in implanted wound tubes on GH, a laboratory surrogate for repair.
blocks.sourceNote: Rudman 1990 · Papadakis 1996

stat.label: rise in skin thickness in 12 older men given growth hormone for six months (1990)

blocks.title: Mechanism, human evidence or open question?
blocks.narration: Six things you will hear about growth hormone and skin, each accurate as worded. Before you see the answer, decide what kind of statement each one is.
blocks.sourceNote: Tavakkol 1992 · Lange 2001 · Breederveld 2014 (Cochrane) · Horesh 2023 · Ben-Shlomo & Melmed 2006

blocks.title: Deficiency is a diagnosis. Decline is ageing.
blocks.narration: Here the physiology meets the waiting room. A patient in their fifties has read that growth hormone falls with age and asks whether topping it up would help their skin. The trials in healthy older adults answer that. Pooled, they show about two kilograms less fat and two kilograms more lean mass, with more swelling, joint pain, carpal tunnel symptoms and a drift towards diabetes, while strength and stamina change little. Graded on those trials the evidence is B, consistent and independent though small, and the Aesthetic and Regenerative Endocrinology guide gives its advice against treatment an A. Both land in the same place. Growth hormone treats a diagnosed deficiency and a short list of approved conditions. In the United States, distributing it for anti-ageing is a federal offence. Whatever your role, name the decline for what it is, a normal part of ageing.
blocks.sourceNote: Liu 2007 · Blackman 2002 · 21 U.S.C. 333(e) · Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology, ch. 14 · Genotropin UK SmPC · Misuse of Drugs Act 1971, Sch. 2

blocks.title: 'Low for my age.'
blocks.narration: One question to close lesson 6.1.
blocks.sourceNote: Lesson 6.1

quiz.prompt: Fictional chart note: a healthy 58-year-old asks for growth hormone 'for her skin' after an online test reported her IGF-1 as 'below the range for a 30-year-old'. She has no pituitary history. What does the evidence support?

blocks.title: One axis, four ways in.
blocks.narration: Four routes lead into the same axis, and patients rarely know which one they are on. Somatropin is growth hormone itself, made by recombinant technology. GHRH analogues, sermorelin, tesamorelin and CJC-1295, press on the pituitary's releasing-hormone receptor, so the gland releases its own growth hormone in pulses. Ghrelin-receptor agonists, ipamorelin, GHRP-2, GHRP-6 and the oral compound ibutamoren, press on a second pituitary receptor. IGF-1 analogues such as IGF-1 LR3 skip the pituitary and act on the IGF-1 receptor directly. Every route ends at that same receptor, which is why lesson three treats their risks together. Clinics often sell all of these as one family with one promise. Keep them apart, because the trials, the approvals and the side-effects belong to each molecule separately.
blocks.sourceNote: Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology, ch. 3 · Peptide Pocket Guide, growth-hormone axis · Dominikowski 2026

blocks.title: What real peptide evidence looks like.
blocks.narration: Tesamorelin is the instructive exception on this axis. Both Hormonaly guides grade it A, for one indication. Read the record in order.
blocks.sourceNote: Falutz 2007, 2010 · EGRIFTA WR prescribing information (DailyMed, August 2026) · MHRA Products database (searched 25 Sep 2026)

blocks.title: Zero skin trials.
blocks.narration: A PubMed search in September 2026 found no randomized trial with a skin outcome for tesamorelin, CJC-1295, ipamorelin or IGF-1 LR3. The nearest is a 1997 study of a GHRH(1-29) analogue related to sermorelin, in 19 older adults. Skin thickness measured by caliper rose after 16 weeks, compared with a placebo lead-in rather than a parallel control group.
blocks.sourceNote: PubMed search, 24 Sep 2026 · Khorram 1997 · Dominikowski 2026

stat.label: randomized trials with a skin outcome for tesamorelin, CJC-1295, ipamorelin or IGF-1 LR3 (PubMed, September 2026)

blocks.title: Name the indication before the molecule.
blocks.narration: Imagine the request as it usually arrives. A patient says their clinic offers a peptide that raises growth hormone naturally, for skin and sleep, and asks what you think. Three answers come before anything else. First, which molecule, exactly, because CJC-1295 with and without its albumin-binding tail are two different products, and only the version with the tail has been tested in people. Second, what stands behind it. Tesamorelin has approval-grade trials for visceral fat in people with HIV, and the rest stop at hormone levels or have never been studied in humans. Third, where it stands in the United States today, read off FDA's live lists. As of September 2026, none of the growth-hormone secretagogues sits on the 503A bulks list.

blocks.title: What too much growth hormone looks like.
blocks.narration: Excess growth hormone leaves visible marks on skin and soft tissue, and noticing them early matters. In acromegaly, glycosaminoglycan deposits and oedema thicken the face, hands and feet, so features look puffy and coarse. The skin turns oily with large pores, sweating increases, and skin tags and acanthosis nigricans appear. Hands and feet enlarge slowly, and the jaw widens. Drugs on this axis bring their own signs, usually transient, with swelling, joint pain, tingling fingers and carpal tunnel symptoms. On somatropin, the label asks for existing moles to be watched for growth or malignant change. The Endocrine Society recommends measuring IGF-1 when typical acral and facial features are present, and suggests it when several associated conditions cluster. For most of you the job is recognition and referral, and the diagnosis belongs to endocrinology.
blocks.sourceNote: Ben-Shlomo & Melmed 2006 · Endocrine Society guideline 2014 · Acromegaly consensus 2024 · somatropin label

blocks.title: Does raising IGF-1 cause cancer?
blocks.narration: The honest answer has four parts, and each has its own source. Keep them apart, or a mechanism will be heard as a measured risk.
blocks.sourceNote: Renehan 2004 · Knuppel 2020 · Dal 2018 · Swerdlow 2017 · Boguszewski 2022 · Guevara-Aguirre 2011

blocks.title: Half the patients on the approved one.
blocks.narration: Tesamorelin is the best-studied peptide on this axis. In its pivotal trials, 47% of treated patients had IGF-1 more than two standard deviations above the mean at 26 weeks, and 36% more than three. Its label states that the effects of prolonged IGF-1 elevation are unknown. For unapproved secretagogues bought for skin, nobody has published the equivalent figure.
blocks.sourceNote: EGRIFTA WR prescribing information, section 5.2 (DailyMed, August 2026)

stat.label: of tesamorelin-treated patients with IGF-1 above +2 SD at 26 weeks in its pivotal trials

blocks.title: Tight rings, eight months into 'CJC/ipa'.
blocks.narration: This patient is fictional, built from the lesson's evidence. She is fifty-two and has injected a clinic-supplied product labelled CJC-1295 and ipamorelin for eight months, for skin and recovery. Her rings no longer fit. Her face and hands look puffy, her fingers tingle at night, she sweats more than she used to, and small skin tags have appeared on her neck. She likes her skin and asks for a stronger version. Read the cluster before the request. Swollen hands and face, tingling, sweating and new skin tags together make up the soft-tissue pattern of growth-hormone excess, and carpal tunnel symptoms and heavy sweating are among the conditions that prompt an IGF-1 test. Neither peptide has a skin trial behind it. Choose the move you would make first.

modules.title: Evidence, regulation and compliance
modules.objective: By the end, you can apply statutory drug compounding frameworks, quality assurance standards, and GRADE criteria to establish compliant, evidence-graded clinical practices in aesthetic endocrinology.

blocks.title: Grade it, check it, write it down.
blocks.narration: This last module turns the course into three habits. You will rate the certainty behind a claim with GRADE, read a compounding status and a certificate of analysis for what they do and do not prove, and write the consent and chart note that an unapproved product needs. The regulatory detail is given for the US in the lesson text, and for the UK, the EU, Portugal, Brazil and the UAE in each moment's regulatory note; lesson 7.2 covers the routes for unlicensed medicines and the rules on selling and advertising peptides outside the US.

blocks.title: Evidence, regulation and compliance
blocks.sourceNote: Guyatt 2008 · Balshem 2011 · Core GRADE 2025 · Hormonaly guides

blocks.title: GRADE rates certainty in an effect, one outcome at a time.
blocks.narration: Every claim you hear about a skin peptide carries a hidden question. How sure can we be? GRADE answers it with four levels of certainty, from high to very low. The rating belongs to a body of evidence for one outcome, such as wrinkle depth at twelve weeks, and never to a single study or to the molecule itself. Randomized trials start high and observational studies start low. From there, certainty drops for five reasons you can name, which are risk of bias, inconsistency between trials, indirectness, imprecision, and suspected publication bias. It can occasionally rise, for example when an effect is very large. Both Hormonaly guides print a letter from A to D beside each use. Read those letters as the same four levels, adapted. They rate the evidence for that use, and they say nothing about whether a product is legal.
blocks.sourceNote: Guyatt 2008 · Balshem 2011 · Core GRADE 2025 · Hormonaly guides

blocks.title: Sponsored studies come out better.
blocks.narration: A Cochrane methodology review brought together 75 papers, each comparing studies sponsored by the manufacturer with studies funded in other ways. Industry-sponsored drug and device studies more often reported favourable efficacy results and favourable conclusions, and the difference was not explained by the usual risk-of-bias checks. It is the pattern you met with oral collagen in module 04.
blocks.sourceNote: Lundh et al., Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2017 · Myung & Park 2025 · Core GRADE 4

stat.label: risk ratio for a favourable efficacy result, industry-sponsored versus other studies

blocks.title: Name what lowers certainty.
blocks.narration: GRADE names the ways a body of evidence can mislead. Read the four you will use most. Then sort four cases from this course by the reason that most lowers certainty. The fifth, publication bias, is suspected when the evidence is a handful of small, mostly commercially funded studies.
blocks.sourceNote: Core GRADE 2–5 (BMJ 2025) · Miller 2006 · Grönberg 2014 · Mahlapuu 2021 · Myung 2025 · Seiwerth 2021

blocks.title: Two checks, never one.
blocks.narration: Suppose a patient asks whether a peptide works. Start with the outcome they care about, say fewer lines around the eyes, and give the certainty for that outcome, along with who paid for the trials behind it. Then, as a separate step, check what the product legally is. The Hormonaly guides keep these two checks apart for a reason. An approved drug can carry a low grade for the particular use a patient has in mind, and a compound with stronger human data may still have no lawful route in the United States. A persuasive mechanism leaves the grade exactly where it is. Whatever your role, say the outcome and the grade in one breath, and treat the regulatory answer as a question of its own.
blocks.sourceNote: Peptide Pocket Guide, editorial standards · Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology, clinical pearl 3 · Balshem 2011

blocks.title: Three trials, grade A?
blocks.narration: One question to close lesson 7.1.
blocks.sourceNote: Lesson 7.1

quiz.prompt: A fictional serum's brochure says 'GRADE A: three randomized trials'. All three were run by the maker, enrolled 20 to 30 people each, lasted four weeks and measured skin hydration. Your patient wants fewer wrinkles. What is the most defensible certainty for that outcome?

blocks.title: Two compounding routes, one strict order.
blocks.narration: Two routes exist for compounding in the United States, and the difference between them shapes the rest of this lesson. Under section 503A, a licensed pharmacist or physician prepares a drug for an identified patient on a prescription. If the conditions are met, the product escapes three requirements, namely approval as a new drug, labelling with adequate directions, and good manufacturing practice. The conditions start with the substance itself, taken in strict order. A USP or National Formulary monograph comes first. Only when there is none can it be a component of an approved drug, and only when neither applies can it sit on FDA's 503A bulks list. The substance must also come from a registered manufacturer with a valid certificate of analysis. Section 503B outsourcing facilities work differently. They register with FDA, work to good manufacturing practice, face risk-based inspection, and can compound without a prescription for each patient. Their products remain unapproved.
blocks.sourceNote: 21 U.S.C. 353a and 353b · FDA 503A bulks page (updated 14 May 2026) · FDA, information for outsourcing facilities

blocks.title: A short list, three categories and a withdrawn table.
blocks.narration: Dated to FDA's records as checked in September 2026. The bulks list is law, changed only by rulemaking; the categories are FDA's interim enforcement posture while nominations are evaluated. Neither is an approval.
blocks.sourceNote: 21 CFR 216.23 (eCFR, 22 Sep 2026) · FDA 503A categories (14 May 2026) · FDA safety-risks table (22 Apr 2026) · PCAC, July 2026

blocks.title: Forty amino acids.
blocks.narration: Since 23 March 2020 FDA defines a protein as an alpha amino acid polymer of more than 40 amino acids, whether or not it is chemically synthesized, so anything above the line is a biological product. On that date tesamorelin, a 44-residue GHRH analogue, and the enzyme hyaluronidase moved to biologics licences, and FDA told compounders that transitioned biologics cannot use the 503A or 503B exemptions.
blocks.sourceNote: 85 FR 10057 (2020) · FDA notice to compounders, March 2020 · FDA deemed-BLA list · Eli Lilly v. Kennedy (S.D. Ind. 2025; 7th Cir. No. 26-1301)

stat.label: amino acids: above this, FDA treats the molecule as a protein, and so as a biological product

blocks.title: Outside the US, 503A does not apply.
blocks.narration: FDA's 503A bulks list and its categories are US law and policy and apply only in the US. In the other jurisdictions in this course, a medicine without a marketing authorisation reaches a patient as a pharmacy preparation or an unlicensed supply made on a prescription, and the prescriber answers for that choice.
blocks.sourceNote: 21 U.S.C. 353a · FDA 503A categories (14 May 2026) · UK: Human Medicines Regulations 2012, Medicines Act 1968, MHRA, GMC, GPhC, NMC · EU: Directive 2001/83/EC · Portugal: Decreto-Lei 95/2004, INFARMED · Brazil: RDC 96/2008, ANVISA · UAE: Federal Decree-Law 38/2024 · read 25 September 2026

blocks.title: What a certificate can and cannot prove.
blocks.narration: Picture the certificate a patient hands you, and read it line by line, asking what each line actually tests. Mass spectrometry checks identity, and a careful certificate shows the expected mass next to the one measured. HPLC reports purity as a percentage of the main peak, which tells you how much else is present and nothing about what that something else is. Endotoxin matters for anything injected, and FDA's guidance says the acceptable limit is calculated from the dose and the route, so a bare figure settles little. When FDA reviewed BPC-157 for its advisory committee, most public certificates listed purity alone, and the one a nominator supplied mentioned no endotoxin test. Then remember what paper cannot do. A certificate describes a lot. It cannot show that your vial came from that lot, how the vial was stored, or that it is sterile.
blocks.sourceNote: Peptide Pocket Guide, peptide fundamentals · FDA PCAC briefing, BPC-157 (July 2026) · FDA endotoxin guidance (2026) · Popławska 2019

blocks.title: Audit this certificate.
blocks.narration: A fictional certificate for a vial of a research-use-only peptide, sold online with injection instructions. Read each line, then decide which would count as useful evidence if it matched the vial, and which are red flags.
blocks.sourceNote: Fictional certificate · Peptide Pocket Guide, reading a COA · FDA BPC-157 briefing (July 2026) · FDA endotoxin guidance · 21 CFR 312.160

blocks.title: 99% on the label.
blocks.narration: Researchers made test purchases of semaglutide from illegal online pharmacies and analysed what arrived. The three vials that were delivered were all judged probably substandard or falsified: purity measured 7.7–14.4% against the 99% printed on the label, peptide content ran 29–39% above the labelled amount, and endotoxin was found in every vial, although none grew microorganisms.
blocks.sourceNote: Ashraf et al., J Med Internet Res 2024 · Peptide Pocket Guide

stat.label: measured purity of online semaglutide vials labelled 99%

blocks.title: Research use only is a label, and never a route.
blocks.narration: Research use only sounds like a category. In law it works as a shipping permission. The US rule lets a supplier send an investigational drug for laboratory or test-tube work if the label says it must stay out of people, and the shipper is meant to confirm that is how it will be used. FDA judges what a product is for by how it is marketed and sold, so a disclaimer on a vial offered with injection instructions carries no weight. The Hormonaly guides say it plainly. Research use only is not a clinical pathway. A certificate of analysis, however clean, cannot convert that vial into a pharmaceutical, because sterility, manufacturing standards and a lawful route are all still missing. Whatever your role, treat these products as outside clinical care, and write down exactly what you were told.
blocks.sourceNote: 21 CFR 312.160 · 21 CFR 201.128 · Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology, ch. 3 · Peptide Pocket Guide, regulatory chapter

blocks.title: Selling and advertising peptides outside the US.
blocks.narration: Selling a peptide outside the United States starts with one question, whether the product is a medicine, and regulators answer it from the product itself. They look at what is claimed for it and at what it is and does, so a research-use label or a cosmetic box settles nothing. A medicine without a marketing authorisation may not be sold, supplied or advertised. Advertising a prescription-only medicine to the public is prohibited, or needs the regulator's approval first, and that covers posts on social media by clinics and influencers. The details differ from country to country, so check the rules for your own jurisdiction, shown with this moment, and date what you find.
blocks.sourceNote: UK: Human Medicines Regulations 2012, MHRA Guidance Note 8 and Blue Guide, CAP Code, ASA · EU: Directives 2001/83/EC and 2010/13/EU · Portugal: Estatuto do Medicamento, Decreto-Lei 238/2015 · Brazil: Laws 6.360/1976 and 9.294/1996, RDC 96/2008, RDC 907/2024, ANVISA, CFM 2.336/2023 · UAE: Federal Decree-Law 38/2024, EDE, DHA · read 25 September 2026

quiz.prompt: A patient shows you the certificate for a research-use-only peptide she injects: 99.1% purity by HPLC with a chromatogram, the correct mass by mass spectrometry, and a lot number that matches her vial. What does it establish?

blocks.title: Off-label needs a label.
blocks.narration: Off-label is the phrase to get right first. FDA uses it for an approved drug prescribed outside its labelling, which prescribers generally may do when they judge it medically appropriate. The idea assumes a label exists. A peptide that was never approved has none, so prescribing it counts as using an unapproved drug, and the Peptide Pocket Guide says exactly that. Compounding leaves that answer unchanged. A compounded product is unapproved by definition, and it is lawful only when the substance and the pharmacy meet the statute's conditions. Under federal law, putting an unapproved new drug into interstate commerce is a prohibited act, and in 2020 FDA warned a compounding pharmacy about its BPC-157 and GHK-Cu products on that basis. So write the real category in the chart, every time.
blocks.sourceNote: FDA, unapproved use of approved drugs · 21 U.S.C. 331 · FDA warning letter, Tailor Made Compounding (2020) · Peptide Pocket Guide

blocks.title: Same molecule, different rulebooks.

blocks.title: 'Just prescribe it off-label.'
blocks.narration: A fictional patient, built from this module's sources, is fifty-two and three weeks past a fractional laser treatment. She asks you to prescribe compounded BPC-157 injections off-label to speed her healing. A pharmacy is willing to make it, and she shows you its certificate of analysis. Three facts shape your answer. BPC-157 has never been approved, so there is no label to prescribe around. It has no 503A route, its nominations were withdrawn, and FDA's own reviewers advised against listing it in July 2026, noting a lack of evidence that it works even for the condition they studied. And a certificate describes a batch, which leaves sterility and legality exactly where they were. Decide how you will answer her.

check.prompt: Closing Module 7: which statement keeps evidence, regulatory status and product quality apart?

options.text: The certificate shows 99% purity, so the peptide is evidence-based and fine to compound.
Topical GHK-Cu: small-trial evidence (C); in the US, non-injectable use sits in 503A Category 1, under evaluation; its certificate can show identity and purity, never sterility or legality.
GHK-Cu is in Category 1, so it is approved for skin and the evidence question is settled.
